title: patch_file incorrectly parses unified diff file headers as context lines
description: When a unified diff includes '--- a/path' and '+++ b/path' file headers, patch_file treats the leading '-' and '+' characters as removed/added content lines rather than diff metadata, causing 'removed lines not in file' errors. The fix_signal run had to fall back to write_file after two failed patch attempts.
proposed_resolution: Update patch_file.rs to strip unified diff file header lines (lines matching '^--- ' or '^+++ ') before processing hunk content, treating them as metadata rather than content changes.

title: fix_signal.skill.md Phase 3 should prefer write_file over patch_file for small JSON signal files
description: Phase 3 directs the agent to use patch_file for marking signal files, but patch_file consistently fails on these small JSON files due to content matching issues. The fallback to write_file is reliable for files of this size and avoids unnecessary patch failures.
proposed_resolution: Update fix_signal.skill.md Phase 3 to prefer write_file directly for signal files (which are always small JSON) rather than attempting patch_file first.

title: patch_file should strip unified diff file header lines before hunk processing
description: The patch_file tool fails when a caller includes '--- a/path' and '+++ b/path' lines in the diff input because the parser treats them as content lines. Standard unified diff format includes these headers, and callers reasonably supply them. The tool should silently discard file header lines before parsing hunks.
proposed_resolution: Add a pre-processing step in patch_file.rs that filters out lines matching '^--- ' and '^+++ ' before the hunk parser runs, making the tool tolerant of standard unified diff format.

summary: The fix_signal run for signal 22a24658-8a03-42f2-9312-712d42f1b22a (Critical: Release pipeline GitHub Actions Node.js 24 upgrade) completed its core objectives: signal marked as picked up, isolation branch feat/fix-release-pipeline-github-actions-require-node-js-24 created, and signal.accepted event emitted. Two rubrics failed: moeb-tool-origin (ToolSearch and Read used by the outer assistant without MissingMoebTool signals) and tool-errors (two patch_file failures before write_file fallback succeeded). The patch_file failures expose a recurring issue with diff header lines being parsed as content — a ToolImprovement and a SkillImprovement have been raised to address this pattern.
